Theorem
[Euler--Lagrange equation for a minimizer] 1. ch8:8.1.2\group Euler–Lagrange Equations Any smooth minimizer $u$ of $I[\cdot ]$, subject to the boundary condition $u = g$ on $\partial U$, is a solution of the Euler--Lagrange partial differential equation \[ -\sum _{i=1}^{n}(L_{p_i}(Du, u, x))_{x_i} + L_z(Du, u, x) = 0 \quad \text{in } U. \] This is a quasilinear, second-order PDE in divergence form.

Proof

\sketch For $v\in C_c^\infty (U)$, the variations $u+\tau v$ remain admissible for small $\tau $. Differentiating $I[u+\tau v]$ at $\tau =0$ gives the weak Euler–Lagrange identity; integration by parts yields the PDE.

□
